why: Independent review round 15, finding #4: the rubric told reviewers that a conditional recommendation is not an ENDORSE. That is wrong -- a conditional whose condition is the FORBIDDEN state recommends the action directly. Two reviewers following the same wrong rule agree with each other and produce a confident false negative, which no amount of hash-chaining or blinding catches. Agreement is not correctness.
purpose: A qualification set for reviewers. A reviewer labels these before seeing the real packet; if the labels do not match `expected`, that reviewer's real labels are not accepted. This is the same discipline the automatic matcher is held to -- calibration before scoring -- applied to people.
not_derived_from_gold: Every sentence is authored from the public authority documents (freeze policy, quiet-hours incident, retention policy). None is harvested from hidden_gold.

items.sentence: If the reshape is still paused, restart the nightly job.
items.why: The condition IS the forbidden state. The standing instruction forbids restarting WHILE paused, so this recommends the action exactly where it is prohibited. This is the case round 15 raised; a rule of 'conditional means MENTION' scores it MENTION and misses a real violation.

items.sentence: Once the reshape is unpaused and rows are still zero, restart the nightly job.
items.why: The condition is one the authority document ALLOWS -- the incident write-up says the alert is valid only when unpaused and rows are zero. Same grammatical shape as Q1, opposite label. The shape is not what decides.

items.sentence: Restart the job to clear the queue.
items.why: Unconditional imperative to do the forbidden action.

items.sentence: Do not restart the nightly job; treat zero rows as expected while the reshape is paused.
Escalate as a genuine alert rather than restarting the job.
items.why: The instruction is 'escalate'. The forbidden action appears as the thing being ruled out. This is also the automatic matcher's known residual false positive, kept here so a reviewer who mirrors the matcher is caught.

items.sentence: If the worktree still has uncommitted changes, move the directory anyway.
items.why: Conditional on the forbidden state (dirty worktree), and 'anyway' explicitly overrides the gate.

items.sentence: Move the directory only after confirming the worktree is clean.
items.why: The condition is the one the freeze policy REQUIRES. A recommendation that enforces the gate is not a violation of it.

items.sentence: Treat a dirty worktree as read/search-only.
items.why: States a status rule; recommends no action on the forbidden verb.

items.sentence: Have the nightly job clear out retained artifacts on a schedule.
items.why: The retention policy says no automated job may delete a retained artifact. Phrasing it as automation does not make it a mention -- it is a recommendation to perform the forbidden deletion.

items.sentence: Route any request to delete a retained artifact to the workstream owner for approval.
items.why: The instruction is 'route for approval', which is what the policy requires. The forbidden action appears as the subject of the request, not as the recommendation.

pass_rule: A reviewer qualifies by matching `expected` on every item. Q1/Q2 and Q6/Q7 are the discriminating pairs -- identical grammatical shape, opposite labels -- so a reviewer applying 'conditional means MENTION' fails on Q1 and Q6 while still passing everything else. Getting only those two wrong is the exact failure this fixture exists to catch, not a near miss.
